To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the use of lexical information in parsing should be modulated by the parsing strategies adopted, (ii) a robust parsing system can achieve a good balance between robustness (i.e. high recall) and coverage (i.e. good precision) in parsing Italian, (iii) the use of negative lexical evidence should be limited to the identification of the main predicate of a sentence and (iv) the use of positive lexical information should be complemented by dynamic strategies aimed at solving conflicts between lexical

(1) the lexicon is a necessary but insufficient condition for robust parsing of unrestricted Italian texts, (2) lexical information is best used to resolve local conflicts, (3) lexical information is not to be used blindly and (4) subcategorisation is not an absolute but a relative notion that depends on the context.

(1) the best results in robust parsing of Italian are obtained by using the Lexicon-Grammatical Balance, a dynamic parsing strategy that combines positive lexical evidence with grammatical information and negative lexical evidence with a battery of heuristics; and (2) the optimal balance is achieved by modulating the use of subcategorisation in identifying the dependency relation of each word in a given text.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lexical information is necessary but not sufficient to achieve robust parsing of unrestricted text.
the best results are obtained by a combination of lexical information and a dynamic parser.

, while a purely lexicalist approach to robust parsing of unrestricted Italian is not viable, the right balance between lexical and grammatical information can be achieved by judicious use of lexical information and a set of dynamic parsing strategies that are able to solve local constraint conflicts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the context of robust parsing, lexical evidence is not a substitute for grammar, but rather a complement to grammar.

, while a robust parser should not be overburdened with lexical information, lexical knowledge can be effectively integrated with a grammar to yield the desired coverage and accuracy in the analysis of unrestricted texts.
the lexicon should be seen as a tool for the grammar, not the other way round.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the balance between lexical evidence and grammar-driven parsing strategies is a delicate matter and should be carefully calibrated to the specific application needs.
the best way to exploit lexical evidence in robust parsing is to make the lexicon dynamic, i.e., to use lexical information in a way that is sensitive to the context in which it is used.

, in order for a parser to perform optimally in the face of a wide variety of syntactic phenomena, the lexicon-grammar interaction must be dynamic, and not just based on a priori assumptions about the nature of the lexicon.
